faqs.question: What is the alpha ratio of {{name}}?
faqs.answer:
The alpha ratio for the {{name}} is {{ratios.alpha}}

Alpha is the excess return of a fund compared to its expected return, based on its beta and the risk-free rate. Positive alpha indicates that the fund has outperformed its expected return, while negative alpha suggests underperformance.

faqs.question: What is the volatility or standard deviation of {{name}}?
faqs.answer:
The volatility or standard deviation for the {{name}} is {{ratios.stdDev}}

Standard deviation measures the volatility or risk associated with the returns of a mutual fund. A higher standard deviation indicates higher volatility, suggesting that the returns of the mutual fund are more spread out from the average. On the other hand, a lower standard deviation implies lower volatility and a more stable performance.

faqs.question: What is the sharpe ratio of {{name}}?
faqs.answer:
The Sharpe ratio for the {{name}} is {{ratios.sharpe}}

The Sharpe ratio is a measure of risk-adjusted return that evaluates the performance of a mutual fund, by adjusting for its risk. Higher Sharpe ratio indicates a better risk-adjusted performance. A positive Sharpe ratio indicates that the MF has provided a return in excess of the risk-free rate for the amount of risk taken. Conversely, a negative Sharpe ratio suggests that the MF did not adequately compensate for the risk.

faqs.question: What is the Sortino ratio of {{name}}?
faqs.answer:
The Sortino Ratio for the {{name}} is {{ratios.sortino}}

The Sortino ratio of a mutual fund is a measure of its risk-adjusted return, considering only downside volatility. It helps investors evaluate how well a fund is performing relative to its downside risk. A higher Sortino ratio (value >1) means the fund generates better returns for the downside risk taken.

faqs.answer: The PE ratio of {{name}} is {{ratios.pe}}, while category PE ratio is {{ratios.catPe}}.

mainEntity.name: What is the Market Mood Index (MMI)?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Market Mood Index (MMI) is a sentiment indicator that helps investors understand the current emotional state of the Indian stock market, ranging from Extreme Fear to Extreme Greed.
MMI is calculated using 6 important factors: FII Activity, Volatility (VIX), Market Momentum, Price Strength, Buy Sell Disparity, and Skew Index.

mainEntity.name: When should I invest based on MMI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Historically, Extreme Fear (low MMI) is considered a good time to buy as markets may be oversold, while Extreme Greed (high MMI) suggests caution as a correction might be due.

howTo.name: How to use MMI for Market Timing

step.name: Check Current MMI
step.text: Visit the Tickertape MMI page to see the current index value (0-100).

step.name: Identify the Zone
step.text: Determine if the needle is in Extreme Fear, Fear, Greed, or Extreme Greed.

step.name: Analyze Factors
step.text: Scroll down to see which factors like FII activity or Volatility are driving the current mood.

step.name: Execute Trade
step.text: Use the sentiment data to decide whether to enter a new position or wait for a better market mood.

howTo.description: Follow these steps to use the Market Mood Index for making informed investment decisions.

acceptedAnswer.text: A tool that lets you filter and discover US stocks and ETFs using 80+ parameters including market cap, P/E ratio, revenue growth, sector, analyst ratings, and more.

mainEntity.name: How many filters are available on the US Stocks Screener?

acceptedAnswer.text: The screener offers 88 filters for US stocks across 12 categories — covering profitability, valuation, growth, technical indicators, analyst ratings, and more.

mainEntity.name: Can I screen US ETFs on Tickertape?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. ETFs are accessible within the US Stocks Screener. You can filter by ETF-specific parameters like AUM, expense ratio, dividend yield, P/E, and P/B ratio.

mainEntity.name: Can I filter stocks from the S&P 500 or NASDAQ 100?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The screener includes a Universe Selector that lets you scope results to the S&P 500, NASDAQ 100, NASDAQ, Dow Jones 30, or your own custom watchlist.

mainEntity.name: Can I save my custom US stock screen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Logged-in users can save their filter configuration and universe as a named screen, and revisit or share it anytime.

mainEntity.name: Is the US Stocks Screener free to use?

acceptedAnswer.text: All 88 filters are available to all users with no premium gating.

mainEntity.name: What data is used for US stock screening?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data is sourced via the Fundamentals API (EOD Historical Data), covering financials, valuation ratios, analyst estimates, ownership, and technicals.

mainEntity.name: How is the US Stocks Screener different from the India Screener?

acceptedAnswer.text: The US Screener filters US-listed stocks and ETFs with USD-denominated metrics. It shares the same UI and interaction patterns as the India Equity Screener.

mainEntity.name: What indices can I use to scope my US stock search?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can scope to S&P 500, NASDAQ 100, NASDAQ, Dow Jones 30, or create a custom universe using your Tickertape watchlist or manually entered tickers.

faqs.question: What is Loan against Stocks (LAS)?
faqs.answer: Loan against Stocks is a secured lending solution where you can borrow money by pledging your existing stocks and ETFs as collateral. This allows you to access funds without selling their investments, thereby retaining ownership and potential for future gains.

faqs.question: What is the tenure of loan against stocks?
faqs.answer: The tenure of the loan is up to 36 months. During this tenure, you can do part-prepayment or foreclosure of the loan without any charges.

faqs.question: What is the process for availing a loan against stocks?
faqs.answer:
You can get a loan against stocks online on smallcase in 4 easy steps – a completely digital and paperless process.
  • Import your stocks and ETFs investments
  • Add a bank account for receiving funds and set up a mandate for monthly interest auto-debit
  • Pledge your stocks with the lender
  • Sign the loan agreement online

sections.title: Nature of Services
sections.content: Anchorage Technologies Private Limited ("Tickertape" or "ATPL" or "Us") provides you access to discover, track, & transact in US securities ("Global Access") via the technology solution provided by CASE Platforms Pvt Ltd ("CASE"; being ATPL's holding company). CASE acts as a referrer to ViewTrade International IFSC Pvt Ltd ("VTI IFSC"), a licensed broker-dealer and Global Access Provider in GIFT City IFSC (IFSCA Registration Number: IFSC/BD/2024-25/0003), to facilitate account opening & transactions in US securities. Further, CASE is a referrer to Glomopay Software Private Limited ("Glomopay") to enable you to remit money for investing in US securities. Glomopay is a partner to RBI-regulated banks for allowing you to remit money in compliance with the applicable laws

sections.title: Confirmations
sections.content:
You confirm and agree to:

  • Your birth country is India
  • You are a citizen of India
  • You are not a US Citizen
  • You are not a politically exposed person
  • You are a tax resident of India and not a resident of any other country
  • You are not liable to pay taxes in any other country
  • You have not had actions taken or proceedings initiated against you in the past 3 years
  • You certify that the beneficial owner is resident of the country of India (only applicable to non-individuals)
  • You are not legally required to obtain a foreign Taxpayer Identification Number in your country
  • No special rates and conditions apply to you
  • You or any member of your immediate family not belonging to any of the below categories:
    • Affiliated or work with a US registered broker-dealer or FINRA
    • Senior executive at or a 10% or greater shareholder of a publicly traded company
    • A senior political figure
    • A family member or relative of a senior political figure

sections.title: Disclosures, Forms and Policies
sections.content:
By proceeding, you confirm that you have read and understood the following disclosures and forms, and you hereby accept that you shall comply with its terms at all times:

  • Risk Disclosure Statement
    This document outlines key risks and advantages of investing in global capital markets through VTI IFSC
  • Trading Handling Disclosure
    This document explains how VTI IFSC executes orders, handles trades, and processes fractional trading
  • Crypto Asset Disclosures
    This document outlines key trading restrictions for ViewTrade International IFSC accounts, including restrictions on crypto assets
  • FATCA/CRS Declaration Form
    This form certifies foreign tax status for compliance with US Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act and Common Reporting Standard.
  • W8 Ben Form
    This IRS form certifies foreign status for US tax withholding and reporting for individuals.
  • VTI IFSC Grievance Redressal Policy
    This policy establishes the framework for efficient resolution of customer complaints at VTI IFSC
  • Anti-Money Laundering/Know your Customer Policy
    This document establishes the Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering framework for VTI IFSC in compliance with IFSCA Guidelines.
